text_fidelity_a:
Food and Fitness Journal Meal Journal Diary Workout Wellness Log Notebook Planner Weight Loss Diet Meal Exercise Training Health Tracker 6.1" x 8.5" Hard Cover I’m far more old school than my wife when it comes to tracking my workouts and eating. Part of it is that I tend to forget to do it if I don’t see it and part is the act of writing things out - rather than clicking and typing while fighting autocorrect.

So I grabbed this Food and Fitness Journal Diary Workout Wellness Log Notebook for myself. In general, it’s good, but with an *. First, it’s all pink. Hey, I’m not hung up on the color - pink does not impinge my confidence. That said, I’m not a big fan of pink and a lot of guys out there would prefer something other than pink. But the same with ladies. My wife looked at it when it arrived and all she could say was, “wow. Really pink, isn’t it?” She wasn’t all that drawn to it. Other color options might help. Second, this Food and Fitness Journal Diary Workout Wellness Log Notebook is well constructed. It’s hard front and back covers are nice - I think they’ll last - not sure what happens if they ever get wet, but what book survives that? The inside pages are fine - a bit glossy - I have a pen that works fine. With the spiral on this, you can lay it flat open to both pages or just one - both lay fine and are easy to work with open. The pictures I provide are pretty much copies of the ones on the product page - it looks exactly the same. So basically what you’re getting is a place to record your starting sizes (body) and data, places to record calories of favorite foods (not a lot of slots, but enough for faves), and places to lay out meals and exercises. In general, you have plenty of room. If you need more, stick in your own paper pages, or supplement with a computer program. As for those calories - you are not given a lot of places for food items, but again, you can always supplement with things you find online and fill them in here when you eat them. Meaning you are not given a lot of options of choices with food data, but with SO many options even today’s dynamic food apps don’t always include ALL potential food options, so even there you’re doing a bit of research at times. And if you’re limiting your intake, you don’t (necessarily) need a lot of lines for that.

For me the idea is that I keep this on my desk and it’s always visible. I’m not forgetting to open an app and I’m thinking about what I want to record - it’s right there. It is old school, but some of us are better able or more comfortable at such methods of keeping track. For that this is going to work well. Unlike a computer app you have a finite amount of space - if that is an issue - but you can either get another or... For me right now, my plan is to use it as long as I’ve got space in order to secure some habits and then I’ll likely let it go. It’s good what what it is - hence the 5 stars - but has it’s limits hence the *.
text_fidelity_b: Food and Fitness Journal Meal Journal Diary Workout Wellness Log Notebook Planner Weight Loss Diet Meal Exercise Training Health Tracker 6.1" x 8.5" Hard Cover

text_fidelity_a:
Coghlans 0008 Camp Knife This is just the right size for my medium size hands and disappears in my pocket. Fit and finish are great. There are no flaws in the Opinel blade locking ring, or handle. When properly locked open there is no play in the blade in any direction. Opening and closing the unlocked blade require a little effort which is the way that I like it. The wood handle is varnished. The locking ring is stiff and requires quite a bit more than my 12 year old Opinel. This is reported to ease up after using it for a while and I don't find it to be objectionable. Shaving sharpness is there too. This knife totally meets my expectations and requirements.
The dimensions of this knife are:

4-1/4" closed
3-1/4" Blade
7-1/2 Total Length open

The best attributes of this knife are the curved handle and the carbon blade. The standard Opinel handle is one of only two ways to get an Opinel with a carbon steel blade. It has a straight body with a larger bump on the end. The handle of this Coghlan's version looks to be the same handle that comes in the Opinel Garden Knife #8. It is the curved design with the size and heft of the standard Opinel. This Coghlan's version is perfect size and model for me. This knife comes in three sizes, "7, #8, and #9. The #8 fits my hand perfectly.

The carbon blade requires special care. To avoid tarnishing and rusting keep a very thin coat of oil on the blade and avoid acid such as are found in fruits. If you want this knife in stainless steel with a drop point blade shape rather than the standard clip point check out the Opinel Garden Knife #8.
text_fidelity_b: Coghlans 0008 Camp Knife

text_fidelity_a: PUNT SURF Non Slip Traction Mat & Surfboard Traction Pad - Versatile Mats for Paddle Board, Kayak, Surfboard, Skimboard, SUP - Premium & Strong 3M Adhesive Put it on the seat portion of a Dave Scadden Outlaw Escape float tube that has an inflatable SUP style seat (dropstitch). Wasn't too sure if it would stick well as the surface is not entirely smooth, it has some dimples on the surface due to the Dropstitch nature of an inflatable SUP. Cleaned the area well and cut to shape. Applied from one end to the other to ensure no bubbles along the way, and then used a hard roller to activate the pressure sensitive adhesive. Let it sit for a day and re-rolled to be sure everything was set well. Used it a week later and it held up perfectly, no peeling, bubbles etc. Even with multiple inflate/deflates of the seat, and sitting on it for 6hrs in the water in 110f temps. The product is really well made, hope I never need to use the warranty or service from them, but it seems if I need it, its there and they are eager to help. Great product!

text_fidelity_a:
Lifepro Waver Mini Vibration Plate - Whole Body Vibration Platform Exercise Machine - Home & Travel Workout Equipment for Weight Loss, Toning & Wellness - Max User Weight 260lbs I’ll be honest, I’d never heard about exercise plate machines until I saw this one. I looked it up and according to the articles I was reading, this is an under used exercise machine type and actually does help loose weight. So I decided to grab this LifePro Waver Mini Press Vibration Plate Exercise Machine and try it. I come away surprised, but happy - it does help me. My wife and I have been active in living a healthier lifestyle and approach with a variety of activities, from kickboxing and walking to weights to... well, this thing. My wife is still sidelined from her severely broken foot, so she has not tried it yet, but I have and I’m blown away by how it works.

The machine arrives in a box that is easy to remove from - all the parts are fit correctly and easy to get out. It is slightly heavy - nothing one can’t move, but it has some weight to it. I’m not sure the actual size, but we can’t fit it under our bed, so we’re still working on where to keep it - but that’s not an issue. There are instructions - I would suggest also doing a little research. I learned a few things from articles I was reading. There are also resistance bands and for your arms resistance ropes as well. The instructions are well done and offer ideas for working out as well.

The unit has a remote so you don’t have to get off or bend down to alter things. I have used it every time - I will increase or decrease the various options while still on it. This comes in handy for severity of the vibration as it is intense and I’ll inch it up or down during the workout. I have not gone very high - I want to say around 15 - and appreciate being able to try things or adjust as I need.

ONE CON: The power cord is short. I have to use it primarily in our bedroom where my wife is currently working from bed, so that limits when I can use it. If it were at least another 2 - 3 feet long it would be perfect. I’m going to move some things around and try to make it work in the living room, but if not... anyways, if they changed that this would be a perfect unit.

I really love the workout. It is... (not) easy. I mean you’re standing on this vibrating plate and you do feel it. The level, the time, going up and down, the truth is, your body works to stay there. I’ve only stood on it and done planks, and both were workouts. I got off sweating. I’ll say, standing on it is less of a vibration to my head than the plank - I can’t go as long or as high at a single time because in the plank position I feel like my head will vibrate off. But I can feel my core working.

I like this unit so much that when I saw a foot massager from the same company I grabbed it. While you can use this as a foot vibrator, I thought to help my wife heal - when cleared by the doctor - she might be able to use that foot massager to advance her healing - but again, I grabbed that because of this company - I was that impressed.

Overall the LifePro Waver Mini Press Vibration Plate Exercise Machine is a great workout tool and we are happy to have it. I feel like it has added to my workout and will aide me in getting into the shape I’m working towards and my goals.
text_fidelity_b: Lifepro Waver Mini Vibration Plate - Whole Body Vibration Platform Exercise Machine - Home & Travel Workout Equipment for Weight Loss, Toning & Wellness - Max User Weight 260lbs

There were, again, scuffs on the outside of the bags but no tears or broken parts.

text_fidelity_a:
Everlast Folding Exercise Mat I had a hip replacement over a year ago, and things haven't gone as planned. I'm still in physical therapy. It's been discouraging, to say the least. I'm only 50, and people 20 years older than me recover better. I've been losing motivation to do my exercises at home, because I get on a damn yoga mat, and everything hurts. I got online to find an exercise mat I'd like more, trying to reinvigorate my motivation. I thought this would be "ok" . Somehow I thought the 2" of thickness would probably be a lot of air along with cushioning. I was wrong: This mat is great. If you're in PT a lot, like I have been, you will appreciate and LOVE THIS MAT.

Other than the excellent cushioning (I weigh 180 lbs, at 5'8), I love that I don't have to roll it. The handles are perfectly positioning to pick it up straight, fold it, and tuck it behind a door. The fold doesn't create a big gap at all when it's flat, you really can't even notice it. The thing doesn't slide easily. It doesn't have grippy material, but for some reason, it barely moved on my hardwood floor, which is great when you're doing PT exercises. A slippy mat would have been dangerous. I can't even think of one thing wrong with it. If you are doing PT, or know someone who is, get this mat. Would be a great gift for someone doing PT.
text_fidelity_b: Everlast Folding Exercise Mat

text_fidelity_a:
MaxxHaul 50027 Hitch Mount Bike Rack Platform Style 2-Bike Rack for Cars Trucks SUVs Minivans with Hitch Tightener I have this rack mounted on the front of my truck and recently used it for the first time on a 1200 mile round trip. It is built so that it is not too bulky, yet is sturdy enough for it's purpose. Assembly was straight forward and took about 20 minutes from the time I opened the box. It does have more play in it than I liked out of the box but with slight adjustments I had no issues with it shaking or rattling.
1) I used the included ubolt and bracket to eliminate any up and down movement at the receiver. This is a bit of a pain to take on and off if you want to remove the whole rack when you get to your destination but it works well.
2) It had a bit of front to back movement at the pivot/hinge bolt that is used to tilt the rack. Since I don't need it to tilt at all, I tightened this bolt so that it no longer has any movement at this point.
3) Since it uses pins to assemble the pole and wheel supports there was still some side to side movement to the whole rack. I looped a tie down strap back to my tow hooks on each side so that it couldn't move back and forth.

It would be nice if it was a tight fit everywhere but it was REALLY nice to now pay several hundred dollars. For the cost of this rack I am very happy with the value I received.
text_fidelity_b: MaxxHaul 50027 Hitch Mount Bike Rack Platform Style 2-Bike Rack for Cars Trucks SUVs Minivans with Hitch Tightener

So I order the mount, my credit card issuer charges me a buck for the monetary exchange, and now I have a 'lockable' handlebar bag, which I wouldn't have if there was supposed to be a mount included in the box with the bag.
As for the bag, the main compartment will hold a sixpack of talls and is insulated with removable insulation pads, about 9 1/2 by 5 inches. It also has two thinner pockets in front of that, for maps, cellphones, thin stuff like that, taking the dimensions out to 7 inches. 10 inches high. Comes with a rain cover zippered underneath.
In my opinion, not an example of good value as there are plenty of handlebar/camera bags out there with more space for less money. But then, how many lockable on the bike handlebar bags do you know of?
And/so give XXcycle a browse. They saved me a world of frustration.

text_fidelity_a:
TITLE Gel World Full-Face Training Headgear I use this for full contact boxing sparring. By full contact I mean it's supervised mostly sparring, and we're not out to knock the other person out, but get good 70% power in strikes.

I started out with no headgear at all in sparring. Got knocked out for a good second on hook to the button.
Plenty of hits to jaws, nose, ears, etc. I felt those hits pretty good.

Then I got this headgear, since our gym started a headgear only policy if you wanted to spar.

Well I have Title Gel gloves, so I thought I'd get this headgear, as I love the gloves.
The headgear, now worn for one full session, really does lessen the blows quite a bit. You feel the hits sure enough.
But your brain doesn't get quite as scrambled, your jaw quite as well knocked around, with this well protection headgear.
I am pretty sure unless it's a real hard hit to the button, you're not going to experience a concussive knockout with this nice little piece of kit.

It does slide around on my face as I get hit, but I take a split second to straighten it out once again.

Highly recommended, I think it will save on brain injury.
text_fidelity_b: TITLE Gel World Full-Face Training Headgear

text_fidelity_a:
LifeSpan TR1200-DT5 Treadmill Desk This has been a good investment. I use it almost every day. I bought it to increase overall health and keep my blood flowing, not as a way to lose weight.

The desk it comes with is not very good. It takes two people to adjust the height, nothing should be on the desk as the height is being adjusted, and the height only adjusts to specific notches in the bar. I will look into buying a better desk to go with it, one where it is easier to adjust the height and one that has a larger surface area. I got the desk for free because of a sales promotion. If I paid extra for this desk I would be rather disappointed in it. It does not wobble noticeably at a high position, which some other desks might do.

The app that is associated with this desk is bad.

The controls for this desk could use some improvements. You have to hold down the stop button for a few seconds before you can power off the device, which is stupid and unintuitive for such a frequent action.

They should come up with a better way to lubricate the tread since that is routine maintenance. I cannot lift up one side of the tread at all since it is not centered on mine and the lubrication tube on my bottle is not long enough to reach the other side. I have no effective way of lubricating half of the tread.

Another improvement would be a dust collector for all the debris that falls off and collects at the back of the treadmill portion.

Overall this could use many improvements. However, these products are still relatively new and the competition does not have these problems solved either. Looking at the treadmill desks available for sale, this is a good one, even with the flaws.

Update: I ended up removing the console to use on a better desk and it worked without having to cut wires. I was able to pry off the hole covers and angle the wire connector through the holes in the desk leg to remove the long wire from the desk. I left the shorter wires in place for now. Before pulling the wire down through the desk leg I attached twine to it so that the wire in the leg is replace with twine. This allows me to pull the wire back up through the desk leg if I want to restore the original Lifespan desk. I am trying out an Ikea standing desk that is easier to adjust the height of and it has a bigger surface area. The markings on the long wire are: E146924 AWM I/II A/B 24AWG VW-1 300V. I looked for a replacement wire that I could buy and could not find one pre-made.

Update: this Ikea desk has been working great. It is much better than the supplied LifeSpan desk because I can lower the height if I want to sit down with the Ikea desk. The Ikea desk does not wobble at the highest setting. I am 6' 1".
text_fidelity_b: LifeSpan TR1200-DT5 Treadmill Desk

HYDRONICA Waterproof Backpack Wet/Dry Bag 30L 8 Gallon with Enhanced Shoulder Straps. (Black) Because of the near perfect customer reviews for this bag I gave it a shot. After getting our stuff stolen off the beach in Waikiki a few years ago I never leave anything on the beach anymore. I purchased this bag for an 8 day trip to Maui. For the most part I used it just as a backpack and left it on the beach while someone always stayed back to watch our gear. Kind of sucked that our full group of 5 could not enjoy the water together so on the final 2 days of our trip I took it into the ocean with us. The bag was never completely underwater. I would just let the bag float within an arm's reach near me.

After getting back to the beach and taking my gear out I saw water all over the inside of the bag. Yes, I was careful and folded the top at least 5 times before closing the clasp. I now have two ruined iPhone 6 pluses and a Panasonic point and shoot camera. I'm wondering if I just got a lemon.

This morning I tried the sink test. Dropped some hats into the bag, filled up the kitchen sink, tossed the bag around a bit, and gave the bag a good squeeze. I could see air bubbles immediately. If air bubbles are coming out that means water is getting in. This bag is certainly getting returned. Now I'm wondering who should be responsible for my damaged electronics.
text_fidelity_b: HYDRONICA Waterproof Backpack Wet/Dry Bag 30L 8 Gallon with Enhanced Shoulder Straps. (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Intex Mariner Inflatable Boat Set Series I live in an apartment in Arizona, and I wanted a quality inflatable boat I could take to the local lakes. After researching my options, IM4 appeared to be the top boat.

Although manufacturer claims it is a 4 person boat, it is NOT true. Two people can be comfortable in this boat, three is pushing it. With the semi-solid floor the boat is stable on the lakes; however, you cannot stand or dance as some reviewers claim. Solid floor allows it some degree of stability, but not enough to stand up or walk while being fully upright.

The hull materials and ores supplied are very good. Boat has a solid feel to it. When inflating it to the max, it become very firm- raft like.

For $220 this is an amazing deal. I would recommend this boat!

Update from 10/05/2012. On my recent trip to the lake I broke one of the ores. The plastic on the coupling broke when I did five spirited rows, I was upset. I had to try to canoe paddle the boat to shore and mend the plastic coupling with some duct tape! Upon returning home I checked the Intex's website for the replacement coupling; it is being sold for $4+ shipping. Can't blame the boat for the broken ore, plastic coupling is the cheapest part of this boat.
text_fidelity_b: Intex Mariner Inflatable Boat Set Series

It was impressive for the price. Stepping up to the alloy M was amazing. The phantom X impressed me enough that I ordered 2 alloy Ms ( one in the 6/1 the other in the 7/1 ratios ). I paired them both with falcon rods and 30lb braid. I've got older curado reels on all-star rods with mono line. These alloy Ms were easy to set up, I've never cast a buzz bait so far. The other rod was rigged with a fluke swim Jr and I could easily cast it to docks and structure. I fished a whole Saturday with only those 2 combos. I picked up the phantom x on the piscifun rod, man it felt heavy compared to the other 2. But it is a medium/heavy rod compared to the falcons medium. I've got 7 bait casting rods on the boat now, but I'll mainly be fishing these Ms with the falcon rods. I might in the future step up to the top tier reel, but these Ms throw the lure further than I've ever been able to with other equipment. Great little reels, just lube them up before going out with them.

(Update)
Both of these reels became very stiff to release to cast at the beginning of this year. One doesn't trip the release upon trying to crank back in. So I guess they are good for one to two seasons

text_fidelity_a: Rough Rider Folder Denim Micarta RR2181 I have a soft spot for traditional folding knives.  And Wharncliffes.. This is both.  It's also a good quality, super sharp, stainless slipjoint folder with a half stop and a Micarta handle.  For 20 bucks (or at least that's around what I paid for it).  This knife is at  a sweet spot in terms of size.  Any larger and it would start to need a clip and sort of cease to be "pocket friendly".  I mean what else can I say.. For some folks, half stops are a must.  I generally find them irritating and that may be my only gripe with this blade.  The nail nicks are too sharp to put half stops in this blade.  The blade starts to shift into the half stop and the nick twists and sometimes breaks the edge of my thumbnail.  I thought I was imagining this so i tried it with my pointer finger and sure enough, after pulling the blade a few times, the edge of my fingernail would break.  I may file or polish the edge of the nick a bit and that would solve the issue.  The blade sticks out enough that I can just grab it most of the time without the nail nick. Overall this knife will be a great work knife and would delight any wood worker.

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Big Basin Cold-Weather Sleeping Bag, 15°F Big & Tall Camping Sleeping Bag for Adults, Adjustable Hood and Fleece-Lined Footbox for Warmth and Ventilation, Fits Adults up to 6ft 6in Tall I was an Eagle Scout and we've used these bags a few times in temps down to freezing, and they work great if you get a fleece bag liner and put it in there. We were really nice and toasty warm.

PROS:
- HUGE - really really big. I'm 6ft and not small, and there's loads of extra room. If you don't like being cramped, look no further.
- WARM - It's actually pretty darn warm on it's own.
- GOOD ZIPPERS - they're on the left if you're laying in the bag, and they work well without getting caught a lot.
- TWO ZIPPERS - One down the side and one on the bottom. Why is this good? Zippers tend to have issues going around corners, and this seems to help.
- ZIPPER DRAFT TUBE - Huh? They made an extra...insulated tube of fabric next to the zippers running lengthwise that helps keep air out. And it's made of tougher material almost like a backpack which means...drum roll...the zipper finally doesn't get caught on the bag itself!!!
- GOOD HOOD - The hood is really nice and roomy, like put a full size pillow in it roomy. If you sinch it up with the draw string you can have a face-size opening.
- FLEECE FOOT - the inside bottom foot and a half has an extra layer of warm fleece.
- BURROW - I like to kind of burrow down in a sleeping bag and there's so much room you can bend your legs, sleep on your side, have your arm curled under your head, and there's just so much room. I can put my fee at the very bottom and have the opening above my head.
- LOOKS COOL - I know, it's a sleeping bag and how cool do you expect it to look, really? But it really does look pretty cool.

CONS:
- BIG - We put them in stuff sacks that sinch down and they're still pretty big bags.
- NOT FOR BACKPACKING - like everyone says.

HOW TO SLEEP WARMER:
- Put an inexpensive and washable fleece liner inside the bag. There's plenty of room. It adds to the warmth significantly.
- Change your clothes before you sleep. During the day your clothes get moisture from your own body heat. Change before you sleep and not only will you be warmer, having clean clothes inside the bag makes it stay cleaner.
- Don't over-dress. Start off in like shorts and a t-shirt, no socks, and you'll be warm without sweating. If you start off too warm, you'll build up heat, sweat, and then be colder.
- Put your extra layers down in the foot. Got a sweatshirt you'll probably wear in the morning? Shove it down in the foot. There's room, and it'll be warm when you're ready for it in the morning.
- Wear a beanie, helps with heat loss on your head if you stick your head out for fresh air.

FLEECE LINER:
We used something like this (though not this exact one) and it gets even warmer.
https://www.amazon.com/Stansport-Fleece-Sleeping-Bag-Red/dp/B002YXITMW/ref=sr_1_7?dchild=1&keywords=fleece+sleeping+bag+liner&qid=1592870476&sr=8-7

STUFF SACK:
We used a compression stuff sack like this and were able to fit the sleeping bag and the fleece liner in it together.
https://www.amazon.com/Lewis-N-Clark-Compression-Drawstring/dp/B079JRVVD1/ref=sr_1_4?dchild=1&keywords=lewis+n.+clark+compression+sack&qid=1592870350&sr=8-4
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Big Basin Cold-Weather Sleeping Bag, 15°F Big & Tall Camping Sleeping Bag for Adults, Adjustable Hood and Fleece-Lined Footbox for Warmth and Ventilation, Fits Adults up to 6ft 6in Tall

This is my first bike after about 10 years. Overall I am pleased with the bike.

Cons:
- It runs on the heavier side and you can feel the weight, but I could not find anything much lighter in similar dollar range. Again it's not too heavy. I carried the bike after an accident for about 2 miles.
- Carrying the bike isn't the easiest. I wish the ergonomics allowed for that better.
- Seat could be a little softer but it's not the bike's fault. You can easily find a better seat. I have used the seat for longer rides and it gets painful after about 2 hours for me. So not bad at all.

Pros:
- The brakes are really good. They can bring you to a halt in a pretty high grade descent really fast if you need that to happen. Of course they need tuning and maintenance like anything else.
- The handlebars are very comfortable. I loved the overall handling of the bike.
- Riding it is fun. I went for a 5 hour ride. The bike maintained it's fun except the hard seat.
- Giantnerd's ready to ride made it possible to get this bike rolling out in 20 mins. Highly recommended.

Overall, I would highly recommend this bike to someone who is new, is on budget or needs a bike for daily commute and occasional long rides. So basically everyone except pros could use this bike.

QOGIR Resistance Trainer for Disc Golf, Practice Backhand or Forehand Throws to Improve Your Disc Golf Technique, Increase Strength in Your Pull Through, Gain Extra Distance, Disc Shaped Grip. A little background: I'm a righty, but due to disc-elbow problems (tennis elbow for disc golfers) I'm training my left arm to throw. The control issues are coming around, however so far I'm only getting about half the distance. When I started with the right arm years ago I noticed growth in the muscle over time as my distance improved. Hence my interest in this training device for the left arm. I want to quickly get back to the same success with the left arm.

I hooked this up to a couple of wall studs in my partially finished basement. After using it several times I can tell it's giving the arm a workout. I tried all three band combinations and can definitely tell the difference.

One concern is that the tension on the disc requires a very firm grip. Fortunately the device comes with a safety strap to keep the disc attached to your arm should your grip slip. My concern is that it might teach me to grip more firmly than needed on the course. I think I can adjust for that, so it may be a non-concern.

If you don't have something firm to attach to like a tree or a wall stud, the kit includes a piece to put into a door frame. A word of caution is to only use this from the side of the door where you would be pulling the door shut. You definitely don't want the door to open while you have the disc pulled back in full tension and have that door piece come flying at you.

My only complaint is that I found no instructions. It is possible that I overlooked them in the box and tossed them out. I was able to find what I needed in the Amazon description.

I'm betting that the next few weeks will see an improvement in my lefty distance!
text_fidelity_b: QOGIR Resistance Trainer for Disc Golf, Practice Backhand or Forehand Throws to Improve Your Disc Golf Technique, Increase Strength in Your Pull Through, Gain Extra Distance, Disc Shaped Grip.

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Pop-Up Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 2/4 Person Tent Sets Up in 10 Seconds, Includes Pre-Assembled Poles, Adjustable Rainfly, and Taped Floor Seams I picked up the 2 person version of this tent with the hopes that if would be a good tent for my 11 year old to use for camping. I was pleasantly surprised by how roomy the tent is for a 2 person tent. Two people can comfortably lay sided by side in this tent with out issue. As others have suggested be careful taking it down, watch some youtube videos to see just how to do it as the instructions on the package are not the best for demonstrating it and if you don't do it right you could easily snap one of the poles.

Pros:
-This tent does go up in 10 seconds like the packaging suggests, though it may take you an additional minute to stake it in.
-Very roomy for a 2 person tent.
-Once you learn how to take it down it only takes about 20 seconds to go from being fully assembled to being in its bag.
-I used this tent in moderate rain and had no issues water in the tent.
-While the tent does not come with a foot print for it the bag the tent comes in has plenty of room to also hold a foot print.

Cons:
-You must take it down just right so you don't twist the poles the wrong way and snap them, be sure to practice this several times before going camping with it.
-You need to have some height to be able to take the tent down. In order to take down the tend you end up standing it on its side then have to pull it down from the top, as I said at the beginning of this review I bought this for my 11 year old son and he was not tall enough to take it down.
-Learning to take down the tent is a bit complicated but once you learn it then it is no problem.
-The size of the tent in the package is a bit large, it folds down into a circle that is larger than I would prefer; however, since it is rather flat finding a place to store or pack it is not usually a problem. Though certainly not a backpacking tent.
-Due to the tension in the poles that keeps the tent up it causes the zipper a bit difficult to zip up and I am worried that the zipper is going to break over time. There are two pull tabs for each zipper and the tension is greatest on the upper sides of the the zipper close to where the zipper starts (or finishes), I found that if I have the two pull tabs come together at the bottom (middle) of the zipper then I can avoid a lot of the tension.

text_fidelity_a:
Pyle Sports PHRM26 Speed and Distance Heart Rate Watch with USB and 3D Walking/Running Sensor I had been afraid that the PHRM26 was going to be HUGE, like it looks in the pictures, but in actuality it is really quite reasonable in size. What seems like a 4"x3" face is more like 1¼"x1". Part of what makes it look so large is the black bump in the at the top of the watch. That bump is NOT mirrored on the bottom, and is actually INSIDE the band. What is inside the bump is a naked USB connector for plugging the watch into your computer. The connector fits into a little notch in the wristband to protect it, and the bump as actually much larger than it need be.

I had purchased the PHRM26 for it's ability to measure my heart rate. The instructions are a bit hard to follow, and there is no mention of how to activate the Heart Rate Monitor belt. APPARENTLY, you just put it on, and it works. No need to turn the belt off and on. (Makes no sense to me, the battery would last longer.)

I had a heck of a time getting the heart rate monitor to work because I was taking my cell phone with me, and it was interfering with the signal from the band. I didn't like the idea of having to leave it behind, but once I realized the problem, I used a Cell Phone Arm Band on my right arm, and kept the watch on the left arm, with my body between the two. After that it seemed to work perfectly.

Pyle Audio is a German company, and the manual is pretty poor translation into English, one that I doubt was done by a fluent English speaker. In fact, one of the most important parts of the manual was written by hand, is really in the wrong place in the manual, and gives a very slip-shod impression. Especially when you realize that the list price is well over $100! They could spend a little money and fix their manual.

Calling the included program disappointing would be an understatement of huge proportions, and is the reason why I don't give the PHRM26 a 5 star review. Oddly, it REQUIRES both a username AND password to use. In some ways this is neat, as multiple usernames allow people to SHARE the watch, as long as they exercise at different times. But the PASSWORDs can cause problems if, like me, you forget the password you used. I actually had to abandon my first username because I forgot it's password. Leaving me with an account I can neither use, nor delete. Once you get into the program itself, it's rather difficult to really make a lot of sense out of what it shows you, though it DOES allow you to both EXPORT and IMPORT CSV files that you can use in a spreadsheet program, which is nice. That allows you to keep your own records and manipulate the data in any way you see fit.

One pretty major drawback, is that the PHRM26 can only hold data for your most-recent exercise. Meaning if you forget to upload the data from the watch, the next time you exercise you will either delete the data from the previous exercise, OR you will ADD your current exercises to your last exercises, so when you finally upload the data, the current day will show the data for both days. So basically you need to upload your data every day.

The Pyle Audio (the manufacturer) website lists the PHRM26 at like $135 or something close. IMHO that is FAR above it's value. I see them regularly going for $45 - $75 in different places including Amazon, and IMHO that is STILL more than what it is worth. I was fortunate to find this one being sold by Amazon Warehouse Deals as an open package for about $25, and I feel that I paid just about the right amount for what I got. Now, the fact is that I'm a cheapskate, and I'm sure that there are many others who feel that it's worth much more, but the fact is that comparing the software that comes with the watch with the free exercise website LoseIt.com, and it's free Android app, the PHRM26 comes out very far on the low side of that comparison.
text_fidelity_b: Pyle Sports PHRM26 Speed and Distance Heart Rate Watch with USB and 3D Walking/Running Sensor

text_fidelity_a:
Speed Brite Turbo Ionic Cleaner 200SB I have an older version of this produced in 2003 that lacks the convenient mesh basket and wall adapter. And, yes, I eBayed it for a steal. But this machine is definitely worth it, especially if you have (a) a lot of jewelry with porous stones, (b) a lot of sterling silver jewelry, or (c) a lot of jewelry and a strong aversion to noxious smells (the sparkle gem concentrate is relatively tame even to my multiple chemical sensitivities nose). I know of no other machine other than a professional jeweler's that can handle these things.

While I wish I could afford a lot of white gold jewelry, I have a lot of silver. Moreover, I'm not the sort of person who throws out a pair of earrings after it tarnishes. I search for what I want and do my best to preserve it. My skin is very sensitive to tarnish, so keeping on top of tarnish is important to me. And getting my hands very black while keeping on top of tarnish is less than ideal. The only downside that I'm sure would be a downside with sonic machines as well is that it may release glued in gems from their bearings. Also my instructions cautioned to only let hematite sit in the solution rather than applying the electrical current to it.

Now you may have noticed that the speed brite company only recommends something like 5 seconds for silver. There is a reason for this. If there is braiding or filigree or other little mechanical parts to your silver, these may either serve as catch alls where tarnish that is being freed accumulates, OR the oxidized bits that had accumulated in them will, if the silver is cleaned in this machine repeatedly, start to wash onto the shiny silver areas and leave brown, black, or purple streaks. Also, if your water is getting dirty, bends in smoother silver may take on some tarnish. That said, I find it useful to do multiple long cleanings on my silver with some special techniques and big caveats:

First off, when continuing on this long-cleaning silver path you do so at your own risk. I learned by trial and error and thought at first that I had ruined two pieces of jewelry until I figured out how to "fix" them. On the other hand, you will get WAY more of the tarnish off with the machine if you do multiple long soaks. One key that I have found invaluable when daring to clean my filigree or braided pieces at length with this machine is moving the hanging bar smoothly but steadily throughout the cleaning. This makes it much less likely that tarnish will stick back on. Indeed, this is important for all heavily tarnished pieces as well. If gripping the actual item with the clip, then varying where you attach the clip is also helpful. Making sure the water with the sparkle gem is on the cleaner side of things when cleaning filigree or braided pieces is also invaluable, as they will be especially susceptible to picking up tarnish already present in the water.

Sometimes I find an item that I want to resurrect from the dead that is throughly black, often with areas that are braided or actually intended to be oxidized. What I do in these cases is swirl constantly, move the clip constantly, and in between cleanings, wipe the smoother parts of the silver design under running water with my thumbs to wash off some of the tarnish. Basically I use the machine just enough on such pieces as to get the smoother parts of silver partially clean and then use a cloth. Also, I only clean these pieces when I am about to dump the water out so as not to ruin the water for other jewelry.

Now the sparkle gem ionic cleaner will not remove ALL of your tarnish, and as far as I know, it does not deposit any anti-tarnish coating on your jewelry. For this I have lately been using the Connoisseur jewelry cloths. However, if you have any plain old lint-free cloths around, it is useful to run the chains and so forth along these first (there will likely be some loose tarnish) as to save your chemical jewelry cloths for the final stage of cleaning. Especially with the very powerful Connoisseur brand, you can go through those cloths like crazy as they find layer after layer of tarnish on stuff that already looked clean.

I hope that helps!
text_fidelity_b: Speed Brite Turbo Ionic Cleaner 200SB

text_fidelity_a:
SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Presta Valve Tubes, Multiple Sizes I ordered two Sunlite (Kenda) Thorn resistant tubes (700c x 18/23) with removable presta core in July of 2015. I wanted a thick (puncture resistant) tube that allowed me to remove the core (with a chain tool) to allow me to inject tire sealant into the tube.

In the Southwest, we have nasty thorns called 'goatheads' that cause many flats. As part of my defense system, I use: 1) a thick, thorn resistant tube, 2) tire sealant (Flat Attack); 3) a high-quality, super puncture-resistant tire (Schwalbe - Marathon Plus Tour, Marathon Supreme, or Durano Plus - depending on the bike).

I waited a while to see how these Sunlite tubes would hold up. Unfortunately, after about a year and a half, the front tube failed. The presta valve stem separated from the tube, rendering the tube unrepairable and useless. The rear tube got a flat, but due to the tire sealant, I was able to simply pump up the tire, spin the wheel, and it sealed itself.

I had high hopes for these tubes, but I will look for other alternatives.

TIP: One reason that many of these tubes may be failing at the stem is due to the threaded, round 'nut' on the valve stem. The nut is really helpful when inflating the tube for the FIRST time, (i.e., when there is no air in it). However, once inflated to full pressure, I would recommend REMOVING this nut and setting it aside. The problem is that when riding with this nut tightened down on the valve stem, it creates added pressure on the stem at the base of the tube, increasing the likelihood of separation & failure.
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Presta Valve Tubes, Multiple Sizes

text_fidelity_a: Gaiam Pilates Total Toning Kit When looking for 2 lb weights I opted for these rather than more traditional weights because a) they looked like it would be possible to extend all the fingers while holding the weights if you want more length in the arm.  and b) They seemed to have the weight distributed evenly on both the palm side and the back side of the hand.  Previously, I thought weighted gloves were the answer, but they all have their weight on the back of the hand only, which exercises different muscles than if you were to have the weight mostly in the palm.  After trying out these weights I must say that I'm very happy.  These not only have even weight distribution on both sides of each hand, but you also have the option of letting go your grip and extending your fingers out fully while doing many exercises without worrying about the weights dropping.  The DVD has 3 15 minute workouts which are great for either a warm-up into a more lengthy workout, or for something quick in the morning to wake me up and get me going.  The only issue I have is the videography of the dvd.  The camera person apparently felt there was a need to switch camera angles every 5 seconds.  Very distracting. It wouldn't have bothered me as much if I was able to see the whole body of the instructor more often, but I've done the standing workout is the one I've done the most and often the video shoots the top half of her body without showing what she's doing with her legs... and switches to show her feet and not showing what she's doing with her arms!  I'm sure after I do it several more times I'll be able to just do the upper & lower half movements without needing to see her do them, but when you're first learning a movement is when it's most important to continually see it so that you're sure you get it right.  Especially if you're like me and don't get choreography down very quickly.  It would've been better if they just stuck to one or two camera angles and stayed there rather than switching constantly.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Pilates Total Toning Kit

Swingbyte 2 Golf Training Device - Golf’s Most Trusted Mobile Swing Analyzer - Includes Mobile App for iPhone and Android The app that accompanies this and the way it works is simple and very neat. I have yet to have a chance to check it vs more expensive industry standards like GC2 or trackman BUT for the most part these devices are accurate unto themselves and it's user error that throws them off.

It does NOT do carry distance (which makes sense if you think about it, it doesn't see what the ball is doing). If you duff a shot fat and hit the deck before the ball, it will register that as your strike.

It has a very cool animation and 3D manipulated graphic and pretty much all the important info in terms of face angle/path/AoA/speed/shaft lean. All very good for the home golf nerd that doesn't have regular access to the big machines.

Where it falls short and loses a star from my perspective is this: The mounting system needs a good bit of work. I left it in my car on a hot day inside the little carrying case it comes in (it latches to a little plastic dowel) and when doing so I THINK it melted the rubber grippers that grab onto the club shaft. So now it doesn't have enough tension to hold onto smooth steel shafts (like on irons). So after a few solid strikes taking divots or some poorly struck shots that rattle the club you will notice that the device is no longer in line with your club face. Who knows how long it's been that way so unless you check every time your data for the day could be total garbage. Another thing, the cover that protects the USB charging port is ALSO the aligning mark. This presents two problems. 1 the darn thing keeps opening and flopping around while I try to swing. 2 This alignment mark which is suppose to assist in the ultimate accuracy of the device is on a component that is NOT securely fashioned onto the device itself.

Bottom line: Quite a fun and when used carefully possibly quite accurate tool to help you make your swing easier to quantify and tangible. Not perfect but maybe there will be a Swingbyte 3 that will address these things :)
text_fidelity_b: Swingbyte 2 Golf Training Device - Golf’s Most Trusted Mobile Swing Analyzer - Includes Mobile App for iPhone and Android

OxGord Live Animal Trap - Humane Catch & Release Large 32" Cage Best for Wild Animals, O-Possum, Stray Cat, Rabbit, Rodents - No-Kill Bait Trapping Kit - Heavy Duty, 2-Door, Foldable 32" X 12" X 12" This is my first use of a trap -- used for cats in NE suburban backyard. Pretty good product: caught 5 cats, 2 possums and 1 raccoon in a couple of months over this winter. There were 3 escapees.
Some suggestions:
The trap I received was an entirely wire grid device. Older photos show a solid sheet metal closing door.
Several of the clips from critical places had not been installed and were rattling about in the box. In particular, one of two clips that holds the
trap door to the roof of the trap had to be installed or substituted for with wire. These clips are not the sturdiest. One escapee pulled one loose.
I found that it took some practice to set the trap to have a just so sensitivity, and a little bending of the spring catch. It's not complicated, but plan on practicing. Furthermore, desperate animals will dig up enough soil to cover many important joints, so there is need for cleaning and oiling to keep the mechanism working properly. Snow or soil underneath the trap lever will prevent closure.
I also found that the rear door closure with a large clip and a metal rod is not adequate. A small, determined animal can escape. I simply added a piece of telephone wire to hold the rear door to the roof of the trap securely.
text_fidelity_b: OxGord Live Animal Trap - Humane Catch & Release Large 32" Cage Best for Wild Animals, O-Possum, Stray Cat, Rabbit, Rodents - No-Kill Bait Trapping Kit - Heavy Duty, 2-Door, Foldable 32" X 12" X 12"

text_fidelity_a:
Schwinn Protocol 2.7 Mens and Womens Mountain Bike, 27.5-Inch Wheels, 21-Speed Drivetrain, Lightweight Aluminum Frame, Full Suspension, Matte Blue This is a nice bike and a much better quality than the average old bike out there. It has a few faults, but overall, my husband and I have been pleased with it.

I'm partial to the color blue, so I think it's absolutely gorgeous with its color. It rides well. My husband and I ride on a little trail behind our house. There are lots of curves and bumps and ups and downs with hills and it does well with them. That said, the seat is the worst that I've ever ridden on. It is awful! I know the average bike seat is uncomfortable, but this one is most definitely so. It left me incredibly bruised the first time I rode it. I've mostly adjusted to it now and know when to raise myself off the seat to avoid more bruising, but it took some time. If you don't like skinny and hard bike seats, prepare to swap this one out.

It's also sometimes hard to swap gears. When I'm moving up a gear, it's like it doesn't fully swap over and I hear clicking. I have to move back down a gear and try again. This happens pretty often, though not every time. My husband has the same complaint. The kickstand isn't the best, either. This one simply won't hold the bike up on its own. I have to prop it up on something else to keep it from falling. We have a couple of cheaper bikes that we're able to keep up with just the kickstand.

There is some assembly required, which is a negative to ordering online. My husband did all the assembly work, but didn't have any trouble. This does take time, though, and is most definitely something to consider when ordering. (In stores, most bikes are already put together for you, without an extra fee...if in store is an option for you.)

Despite a few faults, we've been happy with this bike, overall.

text_fidelity_a:
Wenzel Klondike 8 Person Water Resistant Tent with Convertible Screen Room for Family Camping It's always a crap shoot buying an item that you have never seen in person. Our tent arrived yesterday, fast shipping and the product is just what we ordered. So, we set it up in the yard. We plan to take this on a cross country camping adventure in the summer so it's good to have time to get acquainted with the thing before we look like idiots out on the road.

It set up fairly fast and easily being our 1st time with it. It is extremely big, as advertised. The "Front Porch" area DOES have flooring material. Some descriptions said it had no floor, that you'd be on dirt - but this one does have tent flooring attached which is great. It will hold our 3 camp cots comfortably and give us space to move our stove, etc into the porch if we get a rainy day, which was the plan when choosing this tent.

Now for the things you Need To Know:

Its big therefore it catches a LOT of wind. Even with all the windows/doors open, it still catches a boatload of wind. The stakes that come with it will NOT hold it. Invest in bigger better tent stakes and lots of them.

The screen roof is nice, get to look at the stars, but also you need to know that those do not zip shut. The only way to shut the roof screens is to put on the rain tarp that comes with the tent. That's not so easy to do and you will probably need at least 2 people - more if it's windy outside. ALSO - you cannot close the roof of the sleeping quarters while keeping the roof of the porch open. It's all or nothing with covering the roof.

Leaving the tent set up over night, the rain tarp was the first thing to blow off today when the winds moved in with approx. 20 mph gusts. The tent is not set up in a barren field, it's sitting between the house and the woods, which says that out in the open that tarp is going to fly off in a jiffy! You will need to find better ways to keep your rain tarp / sun shade tarp on. Part of that is going to be bigger better tent stakes, and maybe a few more guy-lines to give it more support.

As for waterproof, I don't know yet. We are going to saturate it with water-proofer no matter what.

The last thing you should know is that you WILL need more stakes and guy-lines to keep the tent itself up. Think of this tent as a 1 room house with a front porch. That wall between the house and the porch is held up with 2 metal poles - one on each corner there. In the wind today those keep falling over, then bouncing back upright with the wind. The whole tent is not collapsing, it's not 'that' bad, but you don't want to be in there with your walls falling in and popping back up randomly with wind gusts. If you were using your camp stove in there, the wall could very well knock the stove over, or simply fall on a flame and catch on fire. It's a big deal. So we plan to get paracord and solidify those two posts with lines coming out and staked. I might edit this review when we figure out the best way to keep the wall and rain tarp working right.

All in all, still love the purchase and can't wait to go use it in a few months for real.
text_fidelity_b: Wenzel Klondike 8 Person Water Resistant Tent with Convertible Screen Room for Family Camping

Sticky Holsters MD-1 - Suitable for Small 9MM’s - Med/Sm Autos up to 3.5" BBL Living in hot and humid Southwest Florida means that you get pretty darn hot and sweaty twelve months of the year. Since concealed carry became legal in Florida, I've been depending on a North American Arms .22 magnum stainless steel mini revolver for personal defense. Wearing shorts and any kind of shirt allows you to simply pocket the gun without any "printing" issues. No one knows that you have it, which is the way it should be. Until now I've been reasonably happy carrying this five shot .22 magnum loaded with high velocity CCI segmented ammo. It is impervious to sweat, is very light weight, and if anything ever goes wrong with it NAA will fix it for you--for free.

Now however our world seems a little more complicated. While most defense situations take place within three yards, my little .22 magnum is going to leave me out-gunned in capacity, stopping power, and potential range. With those thoughts in mind, I purchased a Springfield Armory XD Mod-2 Subcompact in .45 acp. It has everything that I was looking for but is considerably heavier. Rather than jump from one extreme to the other, I decided to buy a Sticky Holster for my Kahr CM9 (9mm) and work with that first to adjust to IWB carry with a heavier and bulkier pistol. I'm a big guy, so wearing a light fishing shirt untucked with cargo shorts is a common sight here. While I am able to carry my Kahr in my right front pocket without printing issues, it is a little more difficult to draw it smoothly and consistently. And since pocket carry won't work for my new SA .45, I have been experimenting with placement inside my waistband.

I've been using the Sticky Holster now for over a week and no one has noticed that I'm carrying it--not even my wife. It works exactly as it's supposed to and I have not yet had the holster come out when I've pulled the Kahr. So I've found this holster to work as advertised and I've learned to become comfortable with the extra weight and size. Using this holster has also allowed me to learn where to place my new Stealthgear Onyx IWB when I decide to step up to the SA .45 Subcompact. My thoughts were that I would ditch the Sticky Holster when the Stealthgear comes in, but it is such a good fit for me that I'll probably also use it in the future. It's nice when something works as advertised.
text_fidelity_b: Sticky Holsters MD-1 - Suitable for Small 9MM’s - Med/Sm Autos up to 3.5" BBL

Coleman Camping Tent | 6-Person Dark Room Dome Camping Tent with Fast Pitch Setup, Blue I am a Coleman fan. I have used many of their tents over the years. This one is just okay. I am mostly concerned with the false advertising. I think that's beneath them. This tent is NOT total dark room. It's only dark room tech in the upper portion. As you can see from the photo the lower half of the tent is just the regular tent fabric and the amount of light is very obvious, and this is in a dim basement. With that said, I can easily see having the upper portion dark could really help with people like me who love to camp but struggle with the amount of daylight that comes through in very early morning or at nap time, but it is NOT full dark room tech.

I am also very concerned about the "hub" connection at the top; maybe a great idea but seems very fragile to me. I think they would have been better off using decent, stronger poles, and keeping it a regular dome tent set up, which is a super easy style tent to set up. The poles seem weak. Make sure you have set each connection well into it's socket, and take set-up slow and easy.

The verdict is out whether I will keep this tent or not.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Camping Tent | 6-Person Dark Room Dome Camping Tent with Fast Pitch Setup, Blue

text_fidelity_a: SpiderWire Ultracast Ultimate Mono, Clear, 8lb, 3.6kg Break Strength, 330yd, 30 m Fishing Line, Suitable for Saltwater and Freshwater Environments, High Strength-to-Diameter Ratio, 15% Stretch Ok. I see a lot of negative reviews of things, but I always temper them with the idea that "most people won't write rave reviews for a product just because it works the way it's supposed to". Meaning people are more likely to write bad reviews than good. So I bought a 330 yd spool of the 6lb "Ultimate Mono". Yipes. So I'm on the water in the canoe, and I start fishing. Trolling close to the bottom, the line snaps. There goes a spinner. But I figured I smashed something. I hate losing terminal tackle, but we all know it happens. Anyway, I begin casting, and as I throw the new spinner out, the line just snaps! Poof! No reason. It's a 3/16oz spinner. Why did it snap?! Still I try to give this Spiderwire the benefit of the doubt. So I try to cast some bottom bait out with a sinker. 1/4oz, a number 4 hook, and some bait. And again, the line snaps mid-cast? I can't believe it! This stuff is awful! Granted, it's very supple and manageable, but none of that matters if you can't get your lure where you want it and have it still attached to your Reel. Do yourself a favor. Save 50%, buy some Trilene XL, and catch some fish!
